title: I am doing — Present Continuous
short_description: Talk about what is happening now: I'm working, it's raining, they're playing football.
description:
In Assignments 01 and 02 you learned to say who you are and how to ask. Now you will learn to say what is happening.

The present continuous is am/is/are + a verb with -ing. You already know am, is and are — so this is only one small step further. Use it for anything happening at this moment.
learning_objectives: Build the present continuous with am/is/are + -ing
Use it for actions happening now, at the moment of speaking
Make negatives: I'm not working. She isn't eating. They aren't walking.
Spell -ing forms correctly (come → coming, run → running, lie → lying)
Describe a picture or a scene in English using -ing verbs

content.text:
Take am, is or are — the verb you already know — and add another verb with -ing on the end.

I am working.
She is eating.
They are running.
The bus is coming.

Use the same three forms as before:

I → am + -ing
he, she, it → is + -ing
we, you, they → are + -ing
The -ing verb never changes. Only am / is / are changes.

am/is/are + -ing means something is happening now, at this moment — while you are speaking.

Please be quiet. I'm working.  (= I'm working now)
Look, there's Sarah. She's wearing a brown coat.  (= she is wearing it now)
The weather is nice. It's not raining.
'Where are the children?'  'They're playing in the park.'

It is very common on the phone, when the other person cannot see you:

We're having dinner now. Can I call you later?
You can turn off the television. I'm not watching it.

Put not after am, is or are — exactly as you did before.

I'm not watching TV.
She isn't eating.  (or  She's not eating.)
You aren't listening to me.  (or  You're not listening.)
They aren't walking. They're running.
Remember: with I there is only I'm not. There is no form "I amn't".

Most verbs simply take -ing: play → playing, eat → eating, watch → watching.

There are three small changes to learn:

1. Verbs ending in -e lose the e:
come → coming, write → writing, dance → dancing

2. Short verbs double the last letter:
run → running, sit → sitting, swim → swimming

3. Verbs ending in -ie become -ying:
lie → lying, die → dying
Do not drop the e in verbs like see → seeing or agree → agreeing. Only a silent e disappears.

This is the tense you use to describe a photo, a picture or a scene in front of you:

She's eating an apple.
He's waiting for a bus.
They're playing football.
He's lying on the floor.
They're having breakfast.
She's sitting on the table.
If you can say what is happening around you right now, you can talk about your whole day.

vocabulary.meaning: to stay in one place until something happens
to be flat on a bed, the floor or the ground
to be on your feet, not sitting
to make a sound because something is funny

vocabulary.example: They're building a new hotel at the moment.

examples.english: It's raining. The sun isn't shining.
Where are the children?  —  They're playing in the park.
examples.translation: أين الأطفال؟ — إنهم يلعبون في الحديقة.

examples.english: We're having dinner now. Can I call you later?
examples.translation: نحن نتناول العشاء الآن. هل يمكنني الاتصال بك لاحقًا؟

examples.english: You can turn off the television. I'm not watching it.
examples.translation: يمكنك إطفاء التلفاز. أنا لا أشاهده.

examples.english: Look! Somebody is swimming in the river.
examples.translation: انظر! شخص ما يسبح في النهر.

exercises.prompt: Use eat / have / lie / play / sit / wait:  She ______ an apple.
Use eat / have / lie / play / sit / wait:  He ______ for a bus.
Use eat / have / lie / play / sit / wait:  They ______ football.
Use eat / have / lie / play / sit / wait:  He ______ on the floor.
Use eat / have / lie / play / sit / wait:  They ______ breakfast.
Use eat / have / lie / play / sit / wait:  She ______ on the table.
Complete: Please be quiet. I ______ (work).
Complete: 'Where's John?'  'He's in the kitchen. He ______ (cook).'
Complete: 'You ______ (stand) on my foot.'  'Oh, I'm sorry.'
Complete: Look! Somebody ______ (swim) in the river.
exercises.answer: Somebody is swimming in the river.

exercises.prompt: Complete: We're here on holiday. We ______ (stay) at the Central Hotel.
exercises.answer: We're staying at the Central Hotel.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'Where's Sue?'  'She ______ (have) a shower.'
Complete: They ______ (build) a new hotel in the city centre at the moment.
exercises.answer: They're building a new hotel in the city centre at the moment.

exercises.prompt: Complete: I ______ (go) now. Goodbye.
Jane is sitting on the floor watching TV. Write about her: (have dinner)
Jane is sitting on the floor watching TV. Write about her: (watch TV)
Jane is sitting on the floor watching TV. Write about her: (sit on the floor)
Jane is sitting on the floor watching TV. Write about her: (read a book)
Jane is sitting on the floor watching TV. Write about her: (play the piano)
Write the -ing form of: come, write, dance, run, sit, swim, lie
exercises.answer: coming, writing, dancing, running, sitting, swimming, lying

exercises.prompt: Write a true sentence about right now: (I / wash / my hair)
Write a true sentence about right now: (it / snow)
exercises.answer: It's snowing.  or  It isn't snowing.

exercises.prompt: Write true sentences about now: (I / sit on a chair) (I / eat) (I / learn English) (I / listen to music) (I / wear shoes)
exercises.answer: Answers will vary. Example: I'm sitting on a chair. I'm not eating. I'm learning English. I'm not listening to music. I'm wearing shoes.
